name: Blackwood House
issues: Merged entity: the 'Blackwood' surname covers two distinct source families. House Blackwood (Dustin, who is the 'third son' like source Zhang Wuxian; Corbin; the auction house) = source Zhang Clan, while Ep 115's 'Blackwood Clan' (Ingrid's throwing-needle family) = source Divine Needle Family Zhu. The master sheet lists Ingrid under House Blackwood, folding the Zhu family into the Zhang family.
reason: The source's wealthy Tianlu Zhang Clan was localized as the Western-style noble house 'House Blackwood' to fit the adaptation's Legacy House setting; episodes use 'House Blackwood' as the dominant form.
description: A powerful and immensely wealthy noble house of the capital, headed by Jefferson (Ep 205) and known for the loyal masters it retains with its connections and resources. Its members include Dustin, the third son and a friend close to Ingrid, and his older brother Corbin, and it owns the Blackwood Auction House. Even the Great Houses watch its moves, and Zane later leans on the Blackwoods to raise two million crystal cubes (Ep 307).

name: Blackwood Auction House
reason: The source's 'Tianlu Auction House', a property of the Zhang Clan, was renamed 'Blackwood Auction House' to match the family's localized name.
description: The capital's premier auction house, owned and run by House Blackwood. Zane watches high-value goods such as Celestial Essence sell there for over a hundred thousand crystal cubes (Ep 221), and later consigns his own treasures through it.

name: Blackwood Clan
issues: Merged entity: in Ep 115 the 'Blackwood Clan' is Ingrid's family, 'famous for their deadly Throwing Needles' — in the source this is the Divine Needle Family Zhu (Zhu Qianning's family, Pearflower Storm Needles). It is a different source family from the Zhang Clan that 'House Blackwood' (Dustin/Corbin, the auction house) localizes, yet both were given the Blackwood name.
reason: The source's Divine Needle Family Zhu was localized under the 'Blackwood' family name, inadvertently merging it with the Zhang Clan's localization.
description: Introduced in Ep 115 as Ingrid's family, a clan famous for its deadly Throwing Needles. In the source novel this corresponds to the Divine Needle Family Zhu, one of the seven major noble families, distinct from the auction-house family also called Blackwood in the show.

name: Phoenix Crystal
reason: The source item 'Phoenix Soaring Crystal' (also rendered 'Soaring Phoenix Crystal') was shortened to 'Phoenix Crystal' for the adaptation.
description: A rare crystal that Zane extracts and then embeds into his own right arm in a painful fusion sequence (Eps 143-144). Once fused with his flesh it radiates a bright purple energy and dramatically boosts his speed and the power of his strikes, becoming a signature part of his fighting style for hundreds of episodes.

name: Celestial Paragon
issues: Split/overlapping naming: episodes use both 'Demi-Immortal Race' and 'Celestial Paragon' for the same source clan. Ep 1000/1119's 'seven masters/paragons of the Celestial Paragon' matches the source's 'seven Divine Realm experts of the Demi-Immortal Clan', and Ep 919's tower recognition matches being 'recognized by the Heaven Immortal Clan' via the Talent Stele test. The two localized names risk reading as separate factions.
reason: The source's Demi-Immortal (Heaven Immortal) Clan and its supreme experts were localized as the 'Celestial Paragon', an elevated faction name for the Western fantasy register.
description: The supreme power behind the Tower of Sin: the Tower belonged to the Celestial Paragon, and a warrior earns its recognition by passing the Talent Tablet test in one of its three training towers (Eps 919-920). Its seven masters, all at the Spirit Supreme Realm, were the strongest figures Zane saw in the Lower World, yet even they fled from a Shadow Creature (Ep 1000).

name: House Kensington
reason: The source's great Xi Clan was localized as the Western-style noble house 'House Kensington' in keeping with the adaptation's house-naming convention.
description: A preeminent great house of the Central Domain whose members include Robin and the adopted saint-level genius Brent of the Ethereal Spirit Sect (Ep 691). Its famous daughter (source: Xi Youqin) draws suitors and danger alike: Zane comes to the house for her, and Maddox suspects the house would rather die than surrender her (Eps 693-696). It later suffers a devastating attack that destroys its teleportation array (Ep 728).

name: Stone-Eater Bug
reason: The source creature 'Ore Devouring Bug' (also rendered 'Ores Devouring Bugs' / 'Ore-Devouring Bugs') was renamed 'Stone-Eater Bug' for smoother English.
description: Beasts named by the divine kingdoms after they were observed surviving by eating ores (Ep 856). They infest the upper floors of the tower Zane explores: green variants are manageable, while the purple ones are level-eleven beasts equivalent to Soul Sea Realm warriors, and Zane stuns onlookers by catching one bare-handed (Ep 853).

name: Hugh
reason: The Chinese name 'Xu Xiu' was localized to the phonetically similar US-style name 'Hugh', fitting his role as a proud military master.
description: A Soul Realm master of Silverspire (source: Xu Xiu, an Imperial Army general of White Emperor City). Zane nearly defeated him in combat by absorbing and corrupting his signature Apex Dragon technique (source: the Five-Clawed Golden Dragon) with Nether Essence, a result that stunned everyone and left Hugh burning with shame, though Zane knew Hugh had not been giving his all (Eps 131-138).

name: Cecil Sterling
issues: Name drift: the master sheet lists him as 'Cecil Moreau', but the delivered Ep 249 announces him as 'Cecil Sterling' and Ep 250 references House Sterling — 'Sterling' is canonical.
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhou Dan' was fully localized to 'Cecil', a refined name fitting his cunning duelist archetype; the surname 'Sterling' ties him to his localized family, House Sterling.
description: A Soul Realm fighter of House Sterling who faces Zane in the arena competition (Eps 249-264), announced by Master Young with evident relish. He fights with a fan etched with an intricate Runic Cipher that absorbs incoming Vitality (source: Zhou Dan's Magistrate's Pen and Seal Word Formula word-seals), whipping up cyclones with cunning, predatory patience. He came to the arena with motives beyond the fight itself (Ep 249).

name: Myriad Spirit House
reason: The source's 'Spirit Martial Hall', the core institution of the Spirit Martial Sacred Land, was renamed 'Myriad Spirit House' to pair with the localized 'Soulbound Sect'.
description: The very core of the Soulbound Sect in the Upper Realm (Ep 1029). Zane is escorted there as a newly risen ascender by Master Hill and Master Sloan, and his aloof behavior — sitting alone in a corner — quickly draws resentful crews of established disciples who feel the house has been disrespected (Eps 1030-1031).

name: Hall of Causality
reason: The source's 'Karma Hall' inside the Illusory Battlefield was renamed 'Hall of Causality' for a more formal Western fantasy register.
description: A sequence of trial halls inside the Illusion Battlefield, with entry to the first costing five million Illusion Points (Eps 1256-1260). Despite the outrageous price Zane must get inside, and the halls become the stage for the late-series battles against demon-side challengers, with rewards running to ten million points (Ep 1264).

name: Twilight Group
reason: The source's 'Demon Night Clan', a race serving under the Demon Race, was localized as the 'Twilight Group' to pair with the show's 'Ogres' localization of the demons.
description: A clan of killers that has lived for generations under the Ogres' protection, doing their dirty work in return (Ep 583). Its death squads move like ghosts with completely suppressed breathing (Ep 645), and the group remains a presence from the Tower of Sin arc all the way to the late series, when Zane turns enemies loose on the Twilight Group's own city (Ep 1259).

name: Damon
reason: The source nickname 'Da Meng' ('Big Dream') was localized to the phonetically similar US name 'Damon'.
description: A demon-side warrior in the Hall of Causality battles (Eps 1276-1279), fighting alongside Larkin (source: Dugu, whose line 'Da Meng, ignore them' Ep 1277 mirrors). He relies on a hardened crystal armor (source: the Astral Crystal Saint Body), but a hook-wielding enemy repeatedly shatters it, snagging him and dragging him across the chasm in a humiliating panic.

name: Soulcradle Wood
reason: The source item 'Soul Cultivation Wood' (also rendered 'Soul Nourishing Wood' / 'Soul Wood') was renamed 'Soulcradle Wood' as a single evocative compound.
description: A precious wood that can harbor and sustain a soul — in the source, souls can parasitize it to live on for another thousand years after losing their bodies. Zane urgently hunts a piece of it (Eps 830-836), spinning a cover story to obtain one for a ceremony, and later takes another piece from Yolande's hands (Ep 1053); it is tied to his hope of restoring a lost soul.

name: Tier
reason: The source's talent-ranking term 'first tier / second tier' was carried over directly as the capitalized 'First Tier', 'Second Tier' ranking labels.
description: The continent-wide talent ranking used by the Martial Houses to grade geniuses (Eps 788-1079). The First Tier is reserved for saint-level geniuses so rare they are practically myths (Ep 805); Zane's examination performance marks him as First Tier material, and later trials sort over a thousand entrants through the Second Tier (Ep 1079).

name: Compass Wheel
reason: The source's 'Eight Trigrams Wheel', a flying treasure shaped like a bagua compass, was renamed 'The Compass Wheel' to drop the Chinese bagua reference while keeping the image.
description: A flying treasure-vessel the group travels on during the Demi-Immortal arc (Eps 928-950). Zane pours nearly everything he has into driving it, rocking the whole wheel with the counterforce (Ep 930); Max rides and lends it out, and the Ancestral Dragon is at one point left behind aboard it (Ep 936).

name: Miles
issues: Split name: 'Miles' refers to two different characters — Miles Sutton, Felix's loyalist in the Gauntlet arc (Eps 33-101), and Miles Lowell, a House Lowell side-branch sycophant serving Darcy of House Hawthorne (Eps 326-363, revealed as 'Miles Lowell' in Ep 327) — so the bare name cannot be aliased to one canonical. Additionally, the later-episode hits (Eps 525, 566, 728, 741, 887, 938) are the sentence opener 'Miles away...', a distance phrase wrongly folded into this entity, which inflates its episode range.
reason: 'Miles' is a common US name assigned to two separate minor characters in different arcs of the adaptation.
description: A bare first name covering two minor characters: Felix's loyalist who was sent after Zane and beaten (Eps 33-101), and Miles Lowell of the House Lowell side branch, Perrin's brother, whose flattery of Darcy is all that kept House Hawthorne from devouring their assets (Eps 326-328).

name: Miles Sutton
reason: The character was given the full US-style name 'Miles Sutton' for his supporting appearance; no source counterpart could be identified from the evidence.
description: A supporting character of the early Gauntlet arc (Ep 58), one of Felix's loyalists. Ordered to deal with the upstart Zane, he was soundly beaten instead, an early sign of Zane's hidden strength (Ep 101).

name: Lennie
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhu Feihang' was fully localized to 'Lennie', a warm, informal name fitting his gruff-but-caring healer role in the adaptation.
description: A military doctor attached to Silverspire and Ingrid's uncle (Eps 121-131+). Summoned when Zane collapses with five damaged organs and severed meridians, he is amazed by the boy's willpower, pulls the bone spurs from his body, and carries him to Silverspire's gates with Ingrid (Ep 122). In the source he is Zhu Feihang, Zhu Qianning's Second Uncle and a top elder of the Family Zhu nicknamed the 'Sloppy Sword Celestial'.

name: Consummation
reason: The source stage 'Xiantian Full Circle' (the perfected completion of the Xiantian realm) was localized as the 'Consummation' of the Adept Realm; the master sheet confirms 'Consummation', not 'Consummate Stage'.
description: The highest sub-level of the Adept Realm, reached just before the Soul Realm. It marks the ceiling of ordinary mastery: Bob could barely find a challenge at the Consummation of the Adept Realm (Ep 184), the strongest inner disciples have only recently reached it (Ep 228), and breaking into the top hundred of the All Peaks Competition requires challenging fighters at this level (Ep 235).

name: Master Warren
reason: The source's 'Teacher Wen' of Xiao Yufeng was localized as 'Master Warren', keeping the W-sound of the surname while fitting the show's 'Master' honorific for peak mentors.
description: A master of Misty Peak who oversees competition logistics during the All Peaks Competition (Eps 234-305). He is the peak's most invested supporter of Zane, handing out the match lists with a bitter smile, whispering encouragement from the stands, glaring down rivals like Mack, and even leaping into the arena and begging Zane to throw in the towel when a fight turns dangerous (Ep 252).

name: Blood Prisoner
reason: The source's 'Blood Prisoner', a notorious fugitive, kept his translated epithet directly as it already fits the Western dark-fantasy register.
description: A Soul Realm fugitive and notorious criminal kept imprisoned by Bryson in the Lowell Manor cellar (Eps 328-333). His forbidden dark cultivation is sustained by eating human flesh and drinking blood, leaving his body skinless and the color of raw flesh, and his signature Blood Evil Force is instantly recognized when he breaks loose. Injured and on the run, he crosses paths with Bryson again before being hunted down.

name: World Merchants’ Guild
reason: The source organization 'World Business Alliance' was renamed 'World Merchants’ Guild' for a more traditional fantasy flavor.
description: A vast mercantile power of the Central Domain, run by three heads together with an ancient tycoon and a host of elders (Ep 537). It stands alongside Cloud Hall as one of the great factions — owning one or two Relic-Class weapons at most (Ep 724) — and their allied forces are the main counterweight to Maddox's Corrupted Divine Kingdom through the mid-series war arcs (Eps 696-752).

name: Law Storm
reason: The source term 'Law Storm' (also rendered 'storm of laws') was carried over directly.
description: A raging fusion of many different law powers, trapped inside a vast, sealed pocket dimension (Eps 1075-1082). Getting through the Law Storm is the most important part of the Passing the Torch trial (Ep 1076); even Lord Illusion is thought to have been stopped by it, and Zane studies whether its condensed form has taken on the nature of chaotic energy.

name: Gods-Intimidating Strike
reason: The source sword art 'Yi God's Sword' (the God Yi Sword of Heavenly Sovereign Yi Jian, also rendered 'Sword of God Yi'), was renamed 'Gods-Intimidating Strike' to convey its overwhelming nature without the untranslatable 'Yi' name.
description: A legendary sword technique with no buildup, unleashed in a single instant — exactly as the source describes the Sword of God Yi requiring no accumulation of power (Ep 1111). The crowd recognizes it at once after days of study (Ep 1110); Landry devotes himself to it, grasping thirty percent and shaking the whole palace (Ep 1112), and Zane keeps turning the newly learned strike over in his mind (Eps 1120-1122).

name: Cloudswallow Hall
reason: The source faction 'Swallow Cloud Hall' was renamed 'Cloudswallow Hall', compounding the words for a smoother English name.
description: One of the great halls of the Upper Realm's palace hierarchy (Eps 1043-1113). Membership is a mark of standing — a warrior breaking through to the Soul Sea Realm is 'more than qualified' for it (Ep 1043) — and its warriors, including Brock, who bids a Sovereign Stone for Zane's sword (Ep 1057), repeatedly grow restless around Zane until the hall is left to sort out its own humiliations (Ep 1061).

name: Black Star Pickax
reason: The source weapon 'Black Star Pickaxe' was carried over with the American spelling 'Pickax'.
description: A divine-class weapon hidden inside a special golden leaf, the only tool capable of breaking the leaves of the tower's highest floors (Ep 856). When Zane claims it, a connection as deep as a blood bond hums to life in his mind (Ep 871). In the source it is a supreme artifact containing the law of karma, with indestructible characteristics few things in the universe can block, and it remains in Zane's arsenal into the Illusion Battlefield era (Eps 1257-1305).

name: City Lord
reason: The source title 'City Lord' was carried over directly.
description: The title of the ruler of the main city in the Illusion Battlefield (Eps 1225-1231): a female warrior of only the Soul Sea Realm who nonetheless imposed a whole new set of rules on the battlefield and enforces them through guards like Norton. Zane initially mistakes a male lackey for her ('Wait, he's not the City Lord?', Ep 1227) before making her his target; in the source she is the Ji Family's 'Young Master', the City Lord Niu Jin serves.

name: Norton
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Niu Jin' was fully localized to 'Norton', a blunt, solid US name keeping the initial N and fitting his brute-force enforcer archetype.
description: A battle-hungry enforcer in the Illusion Battlefield who serves as the City Lord's executioner, standing guard to accumulate points for her (Eps 1229-1230; source: Niu Jin). Famed for brute strength and a storm of golden hammer shadows, he meets his match when Zane splits his hammer, drives a fist into his chest, snatches the golden pill from his severed hand, and pins him with a blade at his throat — leaving onlookers to declare him dead (Ep 1230).
